items.title: 2.6 Projectile motion (phenki gayi cheez ki motion) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 2.6 with Fig. 2.8, the three boxes and Example 2.5 (PDF 34-37, printed 31-34).

blocks.text: Ab tak hum ne particle (zarre) ki straight line mein motion parhi, yani one dimension mein motion. Ab ek ball dekhein jo kisi height se horizontally (zameen ke parallel, leti hui seedh mein) phenki jaye. Ball aage bhi jati hai aur neeche bhi girti hai, jab tak zameen jaisi kisi cheez se na takraye. Farz karein ball phenkne wale ke haath se point A par nikalti hai (Fig. 2.8 a) aur us waqt us ki velocity bilkul horizontal hai; ise vx kahein. Newton ke first law of motion ke mutabiq horizontal direction mein koi acceleration nahi hoga jab tak horizontal direction mein koi force na lage. Air friction (hawa ki ragar) chhor dein to flight (urne) ke dauran ball par sirf gravity ki force lagti hai, jo neeche ki taraf hai; horizontal force koi nahi. Is liye horizontal velocity nahi badalti aur zameen se takrane tak vx hi rehti hai. Yani horizontal motion aasan hai: ball constant horizontal velocity se chalti hai, aur horizontal distance x yeh hai:

blocks.alt: Ball Y axis par point A se horizontal chalti hai aur curved (mure hue) raste se X axis par C tak girti hai (origin B). A par, do baad ke points par aur C par ek jaisi length ka horizontal arrow vx aur neeche ki taraf arrow vy bana hai jo har baar lamba hota jata hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.8(a): Height se horizontally phenki gayi ball (kitab ki Figure 2.8(a) ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.text: Vertical (oopar-neeche wali) motion bhi mushkil nahi. Gravity ki wajah se ball neeche ki taraf accelerate hoti (tez hoti) hai, yani a = g, bilkul freely falling cheez ki tarah. Shuru mein vertical velocity zero hai, is liye Eq. 2.14 se vertical distance y yeh hai:

blocks.alt: Projectile origin O se velocity vi ke saath X axis se angle theta par nikalti hai aur parabola bana kar wapas X axis par aati hai; raste ke top se axis tak double arrow maximum height h dikhata hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.8(b): Horizontal se angle θ par fire ki gayi projectile (kitab ki Figure 2.8(b) ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.text: Zaroori nahi ke cheez horizontal velocity se hi phenki jaye. Player ki kick ki hui football, cricketer ki phenki ball aur launching pad se fire ki gayi missile, sab horizontal se kisi angle par phenki jati hain; inhen projectiles kehte hain.
Projectile motion woh two-dimensional motion hai jo gravity ke constant acceleration ke under hoti hai.

Aise mein projectile ki motion ko horizontal aur vertical components mein resolve kar ke (tor kar) aasani se samjha ja sakta hai; yeh dono parts ek doosre se independent (alag, ek doosre par asar na dalne wale) hain. Farz karein projectile horizontal se angle θ par velocity vi se phenki gayi (Fig. 2.8 b). vi ke horizontal aur vertical components vi cos θ aur vi sin θ hain. Horizontal acceleration ax = 0 hai, kyun ke air resistance (hawa ki rukawat) chhor di hai aur is direction mein koi aur force nahi; vertical acceleration ay = g hai. Is liye horizontal component vix poori flight mein wahi rehta hai, aur kisi bhi time t par:
Ab vertical motion dekhein. Shuru mein velocity ka vertical component vi sin θ oopar ki taraf hai.

blocks.title: Interesting Information
blocks.text: Do balls ek hi time chhori gayin: ek seedhi neeche giri aur doosri horizontally phenki gayi. Har lamhe dono balls ek hi height par hoti hain, yani un ka vertical displacement barabar hota hai. Is se pata chalta hai ke horizontal velocity girne ki speed par koi asar nahi daalti.

Projectile motion mein aksar teen cheezen poochi jati hain: projectile kitni height tak jati hai, hawa mein kitni der rehti hai (time of flight), aur horizontally kitni door girti hai (range). Neeche yeh teenon hain.
